All 12 item_findings in `native-editorial-review.json` were checked against the actual options/stems in `candidate.json` and the `key_index`/`reasons` in `selected-private.json`:
- Every flagged giveaway (unique parenthetical gloss, or markedly longer/more-detailed keyed option) is real and matches the private key in all 12 cases.
- Blind pre-key guesses matched the key in 11/12; the one miss (q_ha1_p1_8) was honestly flagged "uncertain" rather than asserted.
- q_ha1_p2_6 correctly avoided the "unique parentheses" claim since two options there have parens — shows the triage distinguishes length-based from parenthesis-based tells rather than overclaiming.
- No item treats the private `explanation` text as verified fact; verdict stays scoped to answer-format giveaways, not source truth.

**Limitations:** I did not independently recompute the SHA256 hashes cited as "Read-only PowerShell parity check" — that's the native agent's self-report. The `runtime_identity: "codex/GPT-6 (self-reported; supervised readonly routing override)"` field is an unverified self-report and should not be trusted as an identity claim. Scope is bounded to these 12 of 666 heuristic flags / 4008 corpus questions; this is not a fact-check of trivia accuracy and not approval to import/publish.
